topic: Retractable (click) ballpoint pen: how one push holds the tip out and the next push lets it back in (rotating cam, push-push).
title: How a Click Pen Works 🖊️
principle: A spring always pushes the refill back; a rotating cam on the refill is pushed below the barrel ridges by the plunger teeth and turned by their slopes, and on release the ridge slopes turn it further onto either a short ledge (holds the refill forward: tip out) or a long slot (lets the spring pull the refill back: tip in), alternating every click.

firstComment:
Answer: a tiny spinning cam 🔧

A spring around the ink refill always pushes it back into the pen. On top of the refill sits a small cam with slanted teeth, and inside the barrel there are ridges with slanted ends.

Push the button: the plunger shoves the cam down below the ridges, and the slanted teeth make it turn a little.

Let go: the spring pushes the cam back up, it hits the slanted end of a ridge and turns a bit more, onto a short ledge. The ledge holds it, so the tip stays out.

Push again: the cam turns on once more, this time into a long, deep slot. Nothing holds it there, so the spring lifts the cam and the ink all the way up, and the tip goes back in.

So every click turns the cam one step, and the steps take turns: ledge (out), slot (in), ledge, slot...

(Simplified 3D model, slowed down and not to scale. Real pens use different numbers of teeth and slots, and some have a second spring for the button.)

Sources:
Wikipedia, Retractable pen (the spring provides the tension to retract the ink cartridge; the cams make a bistable system, retracted in one position and extended in the other; pressing the button moves it from one to the other): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retractable_pen
Make:, How Does a Retractable Pen Work? (Bill Hammack: three basic parts, a cam body, a tubular plunger and stop members; the cam is forced into position by springs): https://makezine.com/article/craft/retractable-pen-work
Pen Vibe, Engineers Explain How Click Pens Work (pushing drives the plunger and the cam body below the fixed stop members; the spring pushes the cam up and it rotates; on release it rotates again and strikes the stop members, and the refill is locked; pressing again retracts it): https://penvibe.com/how-pens-work
UMA Technology, How Retractable Pens Work (stops inside the barrel act like small shelves that hold the cam in the extended position; the next click pushes it past the shelf and rotates it into a taller return channel, and the spring pulls the cartridge back): https://umatechnology.org/how-retractable-pens-work
